title: How HPV vaccination coverage has been raised elsewhere (supporting indicator for preventable cancers)

items.text: According to THL, most children receive the HPV vaccine as recommended in primary school. Few new vaccination series start after basic education, so reaching children at school age is decisive.
In THL figures, Finnish coverage is lower than in the other Nordic countries: 80% of girls born in 2012 received a first dose, while Sweden, Norway and Iceland exceeded 90%.
In Norway, the vaccine is given at school during school hours by a public health nurse and free of charge, so cost and access barriers are minimal.

sources.title: BMJ Open 2015: HPV vaccination in the Norwegian school programme

items.text: A Norwegian registry study found that school-based delivery is largely equitable. Information campaigns aimed at lower-uptake groups could narrow the remaining gaps.

sources.title: Preventive Medicine 2015: registry study of 90,000 Norwegian girls

items.text: A meta-analysis found that digital reminders (text messages, alerts to professionals in patient records) increase vaccine uptake, while information alone does not.
High-coverage countries usually vaccinate at school and send systematic invitations and reminders. Low-coverage countries more often vaccinate in clinics without reminders.
